```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
rawdata <- read_excel("C:/Users/MarziaScelsi/Downloads/MARZIA.xlsx")

df <- rawdata %>% arrange(`Pressure (bar)`, `Temperature (K)`, `Flow (L/min)`,
                          `Time (min)`) %>% 
  mutate(Replicate = factor(rep(c("Replicate 1", "Replicate 2", "Replicate 3"), 
                                length.out = nrow(rawdata)))) %>% 
  rename("Pressure" = "Pressure (bar)",
         "Temperature" = "Temperature (K)",
         "Flow" = "Flow (L/min)",
         "Time" = "Time (min)",
         "FA" = "FAs content wt.%",
         "C181" = "% C 18:1",
         "C160" = "% C 16:0",
         "C180" = "% C 18:0")
```

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE

multiplot <- function(..., plotlist=NULL, file, cols=1, layout=NULL) {
  library(grid)

  # Make a list from the ... arguments and plotlist
  plots <- c(list(...), plotlist)

  numPlots = length(plots)

  # If layout is NULL, then use 'cols' to determine layout
  if (is.null(layout)) {
    # Make the panel
    # ncol: Number of columns of plots
    # nrow: Number of rows needed, calculated from # of cols
    layout <- matrix(seq(1, cols * ceiling(numPlots/cols)),
                    ncol = cols, nrow = ceiling(numPlots/cols))
  }

 if (numPlots==1) {
    print(plots[[1]])

  } else {
    # Set up the page
    grid.newpage()
    pushViewport(viewport(layout = grid.layout(nrow(layout), ncol(layout))))

    # Make each plot, in the correct location
    for (i in 1:numPlots) {
      # Get the i,j matrix positions of the regions that contain this subplot
      matchidx <- as.data.frame(which(layout == i, arr.ind = TRUE))

      print(plots[[i]], vp = viewport(layout.pos.row = matchidx$row,
                                      layout.pos.col = matchidx$col))
    }
  }
}
```



# Descriptive statistics

## Data Quality Summary

| Check                            | Finding    |
|----------------------------------|------------|
| Experimental runs                | 81         |
| Process factors                  | 4          |
| Response variables               | 5          |
| Duplicate records                | 0          |
| Missing extraction-yield results | 0          |
| Missing fatty-acids results      | 18 (22.2%) |

The 18 missing fatty-acid measurements are **not randomly distributed**:

-   All occur at **60 bar**.

-   Their extraction yields range from **0.09% to 0.62%**.

-   Mean yield for these runs is **0.23%**, versus **4.02%** for runs with fatty-acid measurements.

Fatty-acid composition was unavailable at 60 bar because insufficient material was extracted. These values should therefore be labelled as something like **“not measured due to insufficient extract”**, rather than automatically imputed.

## Distribution of experimental factors

This experimental design uses three levels for each factor:

| Factor      | Levels           | Distribution    |
|-------------|------------------|-----------------|
| Pressure    | 60, 330, 600 bar | 18, 45, 18 runs |
| Temperature | 303,333, 363 K   | 18, 45, 18 runs |
| Flow        | 4, 7, 10 L/min   | 18, 45, 18 runs |
| Time        | 30, 75, 120 mins | 18, 45, 18 runs |

## Descriptive statistics

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Response variables
response_vars <- c(
  "Extraction Yield wt.%",
  "FAs content wt.%",
  "% C 16:0",
  "% C 18:1",
  "% C 18:0"
)

# Descriptive statistics:
# variables in columns and statistics in rows
core_descriptives <- rawdata %>%
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(response_vars),
      list(
        n      = ~ sum(!is.na(.x)),
        mean   = ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        sd     = ~ sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        median = ~ median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        q1     = ~ quantile(.x, probs = 0.25, na.rm = TRUE),
        q3     = ~ quantile(.x, probs = 0.75, na.rm = TRUE),
        min    = ~ min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
        max    = ~ max(.x, na.rm = TRUE)
      ),
      .names = "{.col}___{.fn}"
    )
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("Variable", "Statistic"),
    names_sep = "___",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Variable,
    values_from = Value
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Statistic,
      ~ round(.x, digits = 2)
    ),
    Statistic = factor(
      Statistic,
      levels = c(
        "n", "mean", "sd", "median",
        "q1", "q3", "min", "max"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Valid n", "Mean", "SD", "Median",
        "Q1", "Q3", "Minimum", "Maximum"
      )
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(Statistic)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-core-descriptives
#| tbl-cap: "Core descriptive statistics for the experimental responses"
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false

library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

core_descriptives %>%
  mutate(
    across(
      -Statistic,
      ~ format(
          .x,
          digits = 2,
          nsmall = 2,
          trim = TRUE
        )
    )
  ) %>%
  kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    align = c("l", rep("r", ncol(core_descriptives) - 1)),
    escape = TRUE,
    linesep = ""
  ) %>%
  kable_styling(
    latex_options = c(
      #"striped",
      "HOLD_position",
      "scale_down"
    ),
    font_size = 8,
    position = "center",
    full_width = FALSE
  ) %>%
  row_spec(
    row = 0,
    bold = TRUE
  )
```

# Modelling

## Model 1

Linear mixed effect model for total fraction of fatty acids, with replicate as random effect and removing observations with missing values:

```{r}
library(nlme)
mdl1 <- nlme::lme(fixed = FA ~ Pressure + Temperature + Flow + Time, 
                 random = ~ 1 | Replicate, 
                 data = df, 
                 method = "REML", na.action = na.omit,
                 # compound symmetry, because presumably the correlation 
                 # between replicates should always be the same
                 correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ 1 | Replicate)) 
summary(mdl1)
```

Various diagnostic plots for `mdl1`:

```{r}
# residuals vs fitted (default), should be uniformly scattered 
# around the zero line
plot(mdl1) 
# observed vs fitted, should be distributed around the identity line
plot(mdl1, FA ~ fitted(.) | Replicate, abline = c(0,1)) 
# boxplot of residuals by replicate, should all be centred around zero 
# and with similar variance
plot(mdl1, Replicate ~ resid(.)) 
```

Estimated marginal means of total fatty acids percentage, at fixed temperature of 303 K and pressure of 60 bar, for flow rates of 4, 7, and 10 L/min, and times of 30, 75, and 120 minutes:

```{r}
library(emmeans)
emmip(
  mdl1,
  ~ Flow | Time,
  CIs = T,
  at = list(
    Pressure= c(60),
    Flow = c(4, 7, 10),
    Time = c(30, 75, 120),
    Temperature = c(303)
  ),
  type = 'response',
  CIarg = list(
    linewidth = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.3,
    color = "orange"
  ),
  dotarg = list(
    size = 2,
    shape = "square",
    color = "black"
  ),
  facetlab = 'label_both',
  ylab = "Predicted fatty acids %",
  xlab = "Flow (L/min)"
) + ggplot2::labs(title = 'Temperature = 303 K, Pressure = 60 bar')

```
Numerical values of the estimated marginal means (i.e., predictions):
```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
emmip(
  mdl1,
  ~ Flow | Time,
  CIs = T,
  at = list(
    Pressure= c(60),
    Flow = c(4, 7, 10),
    Time = c(30, 75, 120),
    Temperature = c(303)
  ),
  type = 'response', 
  plotit = FALSE) 
```


------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Model 2

Linear mixed effect model for fraction of C 18:0, with total fraction of FAs as covariate, replicate as random effect, and removing observations with missing values:

```{r}
mdl2 <- nlme::lme(fixed = C180 ~ Pressure + Temperature + Flow + Time + FA, 
            random = ~ 1 | Replicate, 
            data = df, 
            method = "REML", na.action = na.omit,
            correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ 1 | Replicate))
summary(mdl2)
```

Various diagnostic plots for `mdl2`:

```{r}
# residuals vs fitted (default), should be uniformly scattered 
# around the zero line
plot(mdl2) 
# observed vs fitted, should be distributed around the identity line
plot(mdl2, C180 ~ fitted(.) | Replicate, abline = c(0,1)) 
# boxplot of residuals by replicate, should all be centred around zero 
# and with similar variance
plot(mdl2, Replicate ~ resid(.)) 
```

Because pressure, temperature and flow were seen to be not associated with % C 18:0 in model 2, we refit model 2a only with time and FA as fixed effects. 

```{r}
mdl2a <- nlme::lme(fixed = C180 ~ Time + FA, 
            random = ~ 1 | Replicate, 
            data = df, 
            method = "REML", na.action = na.omit,
            correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ 1 | Replicate))
summary(mdl2a)
```

The comparison between model 2 and model 2a in terms of information criteria (AIC, BIC) suggests that model 2 with four fixed effects (pressure, temperature, flow, time) is able to explain more variability in the outcome, despite three fixed effects not being significantly associated with the outcome.

Additionally, model 1 suggests that flow is significantly associated with the total fraction of fatty acids (FA). Based on this, it may not be appropriate to include FA as covariate in model 2 in addition to flow, because it would be equivalent to regress flow out twice. Therefore we refit model 2 without FA:
```{r}
mdl2b <- nlme::lme(fixed = C180 ~ Pressure + Temperature + Flow + Time, 
            random = ~ 1 | Replicate, 
            data = df, 
            method = "REML", na.action = na.omit,
            correlation = corCompSymm(form = ~ 1 | Replicate))
summary(mdl2b)
```

In this model 2b both time and flow have a strong effect on the % C 18:0. Additionally, the comparison between model 2 and model 2b in terms of information criteria (AIC, BIC) confirms that model 2b provides a better fit than model 2.

Estimated marginal means of percentage of C 18:0 in the extracted sample, at fixed temperature of 303 K and pressure of 60 bar, for flow rates of 4, 7, and 10 L/min, and times of 30, 75, and 120 minutes:

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE

emmip(
  mdl2b,
  ~ Flow | Time,
  CIs = T,
  at = list(
    Pressure = 60,
    Flow = c(4, 7, 10),
    Time = c(30, 75, 120),
    Temperature = c(303)
  ),
  type = 'response',
  CIarg = list(
    linewidth = 1.5,
    alpha = 0.3,
    color = "orange"
  ),
  dotarg = list(
    size = 2,
    shape = "square",
    color = "black"
  ),
  facetlab = 'label_both',
  ylab = "Predicted C 18:0 %",
  xlab = "Flow (L/min)"
) + ggplot2::labs(title = 'Temperature = 303 K, pressure = 60 bar')
```
Numerical values of the estimated marginal means (i.e., predictions):
```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
emmip(
  mdl2b,
  ~ Flow | Time,
  CIs = T,
  at = list(
    Pressure= c(60),
    Flow = c(4, 7, 10),
    Time = c(30, 75, 120),
    Temperature = c(303)
  ),
  type = 'response', 
  plotit = FALSE) 
```

# Detection and identification of analytes in positive and negative mode

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
pos <- read_excel("C:/Users/MarziaScelsi/Downloads/Features positive mode 29-10-2026.xlsx", sheet = "SFE_LC")[2:44,c(1:5, 7:10, 12:15, 17:20, 22:24)] %>%
```

The statistical analyses below are conducted separately for each level of analyte identification certainty (level 2, 3, and 4), on data related to the analytes detected in positive mode. For each level, four Kruskal–Wallis tests are performed to compare the distribution of the percentage of all identified analytes detected in a given sample across the chosen settings of pressure, temperature, flow, and time; each explanatory variable is treated as a categorical factor. The four omnibus p-values obtained within each level are adjusted using the Holm step-down procedure to control the family-wise error rate at a two-sided significance level of 0.05.

When a Holm-adjusted omnibus p-value is below 0.05, Dunn’s rank-based pairwise comparisons are performed between all observed settings of the corresponding explanatory variable. Within each significant level-variable combination, the Dunn-test p-values are separately adjusted using the Holm method across all pairwise comparisons. Results are reported using the Kruskal–Wallis \(H\) statistic, degrees of freedom, raw and Holm-adjusted omnibus p-values, and, where applicable, Dunn’s \(Z\) statistic together with raw and Holm-adjusted pairwise p-values.

After Holm adjustment, no significant K-W differences were detected in any level. Therefore no follow-up with Dunn's pairwise comparisons was performed.

The following is AI-generated code.
```{r}
#| echo: FALSE
# non-parametric tests to see if the percentage of analytes (of each level) 
# differs significantly among values of the experimental variables 
# (pressure, temperature, flow, time)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(rstatix)

alpha <- 0.05

variables_to_test <- c(
  "Pressure (bar)",
  "Temperature (K)",
  "Flow (L/min)",
  "Time (min)"
)

# Prepare analysis data
analysis_df <- pos_long %>%
  filter(level != "Total") %>%
  mutate(
    level = droplevels(factor(level)),
    perc  = as.numeric(perc)
  )
```

```{r}
# Kruskal-Wallis omnibus test
kw_results <- analysis_df %>%
  group_by(level) %>%
  group_modify(
    ~ map_dfr(
      variables_to_test,
      function(variable) {

        test_data <- .x %>%
          transmute(
            perc      = perc,
            predictor = factor(.data[[variable]])
          ) %>%
          filter(
            !is.na(perc),
            !is.na(predictor)
          ) %>%
          droplevels()

        n_groups <- n_distinct(test_data$predictor)

        # A Kruskal-Wallis test requires at least two groups
        if (n_groups < 2L) {
          return(
            tibble(
              variable  = variable,
              n         = nrow(test_data),
              n_groups  = n_groups,
              statistic = NA_real_,
              df        = NA_real_,
              p_value   = NA_real_
            )
          )
        }

        kw_test <- kruskal.test(
          perc ~ predictor,
          data = test_data
        )

        tibble(
          variable  = variable,
          n         = nrow(test_data),
          n_groups  = n_groups,
          statistic = unname(kw_test$statistic),
          df        = unname(kw_test$parameter),
          p_value   = kw_test$p.value
        )
      }
    )
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  group_by(level) %>%
  mutate(
    # Holm correction across pressure, temperature, flow and time
    p_adjusted = p.adjust(p_value, method = "holm"),
    significant = !is.na(p_adjusted) & p_adjusted < alpha
  ) %>%
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| echo: FALSE

kw_results_report <- kw_results %>%
  mutate(
    level = as.character(level),
    variable = recode(
      variable,
      "Pressure (bar)"   = "Pressure",
      "Temperature (K)" = "Temperature",
      "Flow (L/min)"     = "Flow",
      "Time (min)"       = "Time"
    ),
    statistic = round(statistic, 2),
    p_value = format.pval(
      p_value,
      digits = 3,
      eps = 0.001
    ),
    p_adjusted = format.pval(
      p_adjusted,
      digits = 3,
      eps = 0.001
    ),
    significant = if_else(
      significant,
      "Yes",
      "No"
    )
  ) %>%
  select(
    level,
    variable,
    n,
    n_groups,
    statistic,
    df,
    p_value,
    p_adjusted,
    significant
  )

kw_results_report %>%
  knitr::kable(
    format = "latex",
    booktabs = TRUE,
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Kruskal-Wallis test results for positive mode"
  )
```


```{r}
#| eval: FALSE
#| echo: FALSE

# Run Dunn's test for pairwise comparisons only for significant (adjusted) omnibus tests
# Chunk not evaluated because there are no significant K-W omnibus tests after Holm correction
dunn_results <- significant_kw_tests %>%
  select(level, variable) %>%
  mutate(
    dunn_result = map2(
      level,
      variable,
      function(current_level, current_variable) {

        test_data <- analysis_df %>%
          filter(level == current_level) %>%
          transmute(
            perc      = perc,
            predictor = factor(.data[[current_variable]])
          ) %>%
          filter(
            !is.na(perc),
            !is.na(predictor)
          ) %>%
          droplevels()

        if (n_distinct(test_data$predictor) < 2L) {
          return(tibble())
        }

        test_data %>%
          rstatix::dunn_test(
            perc ~ predictor,
            p.adjust.method = "holm",
            detailed = TRUE
          ) %>%
          transmute(
            group1,
            group2,
            n1,
            n2,
            z_statistic = statistic,
            p_value = p,
            p_adjusted = p.adj,
            p_adjustment_method = p.adj.method,
            significant = p_adjusted < alpha,
            significance = p.adj.signif
          )
      }
    )
  ) %>%
  unnest(dunn_result) %>%
  arrange(
    level,
    variable,
    p_adjusted
  )

dunn_results
```
